content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me something useful.

After your fixed base of ≈£940, your free cash sits at ≈£1,960 a month. The buffer needs ≈£420 of that — ≈14% of take-home, which is genuinely doable. The gap isn't the goal. The gap is that your could-save reach is ≈£0, meaning nothing is moving toward it yet.

So the one move is this: set up a standing transfer of ≈£150 on payday. Not the full ≈£420 — that comes later. This is about starting the habit, not optimising it. Once it's running, the pace is a conversation. While it isn't, the buffer stays at zero.

You called your ≈£280 of eating out a leak. A real month settles whether it's that, or whether it's closer to ≈£200 with a few bigger weeks pulling the average up. The number changes the size of the lever.

Checking a real month does two things. It swaps every ≈ for an actual figure — estimate and reality, side by side. And it opens the half of the picture that's still completely empty: timing, patterns, what's recurring versus what drifted in once. Estimates can't see any of that. Only real transactions can.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
